inline_comments.comment: This test constructs an impossible runtime scenario. `StatusByTypeId` is `Record<StatusTypeId, Status>`, meaning the object key IS the `typeId`. A real record can therefore only ever contain one entry for `'storybook/change-detection'`. The test bypasses this with `as unknown as StatusByTypeId` by using arbitrary keys (`first`, `second`, `third`) — all pointing to the same `typeId`. This scenario can never occur in production, so the priority logic in `getMostCriticalStatusValue` for the change-detection slot is never exercised with multiple values at runtime. The test gives false confidence. A correct test should reflect the real constraint (single entry per typeId) and the test title 'new beats modified beats affected' should be dropped or replaced with a note explaining that at most one change-detection status exists at a time.

The new `statusOrder` reorders two pre-existing entries relative to the original: `error` and `warning` have been swapped (in the original, `error` preceded `warning`; now `warning` precedes `error`). `statusOrder` in `Tree.tsx` is independent from `statusPriority` in `status.ts`, which uses `['unknown', 'pending', 'success', 'affected', 'modified', 'new', 'warning', 'error']` (error at index 7, warning at 6 — consistent with the new ordering here). However, since `getMostCriticalStatusValue` uses `statusPriority` from `status.ts` and NOT `statusOrder` from `Tree.tsx`, any consumer of `statusOrder` (e.g., context-menu sorting or display ordering) will now use a different priority than the actual computed status. This needs a comment explaining what `statusOrder` is used for and why it may diverge from `statusPriority`.

`textColor` is taken exclusively from `testStatus` and the `changeStatus` slot's `textColor` is silently discarded. Currently this has no visible effect because `getStatus` returns `textColor: null` for `new`, `modified`, and `affected`. However, the asymmetry is undocumented: if a future change-detection status is introduced with a non-null `textColor`, its label colouring would be silently ignored. Add an inline comment here explaining the intentional decision to drive story label colour only from the test slot.

`getStatus` in `status.ts` already returns fully-formed SVG+`UseSymbol` icons for `'status-value:new'`, `'status-value:modified'`, and `'status-value:affected'`. The `StatusIconMap` entries added here duplicate that icon definition. If the icon design changes, both locations need updating. Consider documenting which consumer uses `StatusIconMap` (appears to be the context-menu `ListItem`) and why it can't re-use the icons from `getStatus`, or factor out a shared icon helper.

The `key="icon"` prop on the three new `<svg>` elements inside `StatusIconMap` is unnecessary. React `key` props are only meaningful on elements in a list/array; here the elements are not siblings in an iterated collection. Remove `key="icon"` from all three SVG entries.

`getChangeDetectionStatus` calls `Object.values(statuses)` twice — once to build `changeValues` and once to build `testValues`. Replace with a single `Object.values(statuses).reduce(...)` (or a `for...of` loop) that partitions into both arrays in one pass.

`(index[dualSlotStoryId] as any).parent` uses an `as any` cast to access the `.parent` field. Looking at the `IndexHash` type, `StoryEntry` has a `parent` property typed as `StoryId`. Use a proper type assertion — e.g. `(index[dualSlotStoryId] as StoryEntry).parent` — or a type guard to avoid bypassing the type system.

None of the five new stories (`WithChangeDetectionOnly`, `WithChangeDetectionAndTestStatus`, `WithTestStatusOnly`, `WithAffectedStatus`, `BranchWithChangeDetectionPriority`) include a `play` function. Per the project's story conventions, interactive component stories should include a `play` function so that the rendered state (status icon slots, button rendering) is captured by visual regression tests. At minimum, a `play` function that asserts the status buttons are present with the expected `data-testid` and `aria-label` values would make the intent testable.

`BranchWithChangeDetectionPriority` is constructed by `makeDualSlotStory(...)` (which sets `render` internally) and then its `render` is immediately overridden via a detached assignment. This two-step pattern is surprising to readers and means the `render` set inside the factory is dead code for this story. Consider passing a `renderOverride` option into `makeDualSlotStory`, or constructing this story directly without the factory, to make the intended render function the only one ever set.

general_comments.comment: The `getMostCriticalStatusValue` call inside `getChangeDetectionStatus` for the change-detection slot will always receive an array of zero or one element in production, because `StatusByTypeId = Record<StatusTypeId, Status>` allows only one entry per `typeId`. Since `CHANGE_DETECTION_TYPE_ID = 'storybook/change-detection'` is a single fixed string, the record can contain at most one change-detection entry. The priority-reduction logic is therefore never invoked with multiple values at runtime. The function could be simplified to `changeValues[0] ?? 'status-value:unknown'` for the change slot, which also better documents the real constraint. If future multi-provider change-detection is anticipated (e.g. `'storybook/change-detection-chromatic'`), the `CHANGE_DETECTION_TYPE_ID` constant should be changed to a prefix or `Set` check and the decision documented.

The exported `getChangeDetectionStatus` function name implies it returns a single status, but it actually returns both slots (`{ changeStatus, testStatus }`). A name like `splitStatusSlots` or `getSlottedStatuses` better describes the dual-slot splitting responsibility. The current name could mislead callers into thinking it only handles the change-detection side.
